domain: Criminal Justice / Legal Philosophy / Political Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of state execution authority through three mutually exclusive readings of the state-killing kernel: retributive justice (execution as proportional desert), deterrence instrumentalism (execution as rational crime prevention), and categorical abolition (state killing as impermissible). Each reading instantiates a structurally distinct constraint with different victim sets, authority grounds, and extractiveness profiles.

key_entities: State execution authority (monopoly on legitimate killing)
Innocence Project / exoneration data (empirical challenge to system reliability)
key_tensions: Desert vs utility (retribution grounds vs consequentialist grounds)
State authority legitimacy (who adjudicates permissible killing)
Irreversibility vs error correction (execution prevents exoneration)
key_mechanisms: Rational deterrence theory (severity-certainty tradeoff in crime prevention)
key_absences: Victim family preferences (whether families support execution; treated as irrelevant to both retribution and abolition frameworks)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The state-killing kernel: under what conditions (if any) does the state possess legitimate authority to execute a person convicted of capital crime
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Mixed authority structure — retributive reading grounds authority in proportional justice principles; deterrence reading grounds authority in consequentialist state function; abolition reading denies state authority categorically regardless of crime severity

readings.commitment: execution is legitimate when proportional to offense gravity (desert-based authority)
readings.authority_grounding: natural justice / proportionality doctrine / lex talionis
readings.expected_structural_delta: condemned person enters victim set only if execution exceeds proportional desert; murder victim beneficiary via restored moral balance; state authority derived from justice equilibrium not utility

readings.commitment: execution is legitimate when it produces net social utility via crime prevention (instrumental authority)
readings.authority_grounding: consequentialist state function / rational choice theory / Benthamite utility maximization
readings.expected_structural_delta: condemned person enters victim set when execution lacks deterrence efficacy; society/potential offenders are beneficiaries; state authority derived from crime-reduction mandate not desert

readings.commitment: state killing is categorically impermissible regardless of offense or utility (rights-based prohibition)
readings.authority_grounding: human dignity inviolability / state power limitation / anti-totalitarian principle
readings.expected_structural_delta: condemned person is always victim; no state authority exists for execution; irreversibility of error becomes structural rather than operational concern

axiom_contradictions.basis: Retribution requires that proportional desert can justify state killing; abolition requires that no justification can authorize state killing. No single framework holds both axioms — accepting abolition's categorical prohibition requires rejecting proportionality as sufficient grounds for execution.

Deterrence requires that utility consequences can justify state killing; abolition requires that state killing is impermissible regardless of consequences. No single framework holds both axioms — accepting abolition's rights-based prohibition requires rejecting utility maximization as sufficient grounds for execution.

axes.human_readable: Retributive Justice Reading (Execution as Proportional Desert)
axes.structural_delta: State execution authority grounded in proportionality doctrine: killing warranted when offense gravity demands equivalent response
axes.primary_observable: Judicial invocation of proportionality principles; sentencing guidelines tied to offense severity matching; public desert intuitions in capital jury instructions
axes.selection_reason: Core reading with distinct authority grounding (desert vs utility vs prohibition); highest centrality among justice-framework readings

axes.human_readable: Deterrence Instrumentalism Reading (Execution as Crime Prevention Tool)
axes.structural_delta: State execution authority grounded in consequentialist mandate: killing warranted when it produces net crime reduction via rational actor deterrence
axes.primary_observable: Empirical deterrence effect studies (elasticity of murder rates to execution probability); cost-benefit analyses in sentencing policy; rational choice model invocations in legislation
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct observable (empirical efficacy vs moral desert); different beneficiary structure (societal utility vs victim equilibrium)

axes.human_readable: Categorical Abolition Reading (State Killing as Impermissible)
axes.structural_delta: State execution authority categorically denied: no crime severity or utility consequence can authorize state killing due to human dignity inviolability
axes.primary_observable: Constitutional challenges citing cruel-and-unusual / dignity clauses; international human rights treaty ratification patterns; irreversibility-of-error doctrines in anti-death-penalty litigation
axes.selection_reason: Mountain-type constraint (categorical prohibition); different victim structure (always-victim vs conditional); completes the triadic reading set

omegas.description: Does victim family support for execution strengthen retributive justification or is it structurally irrelevant? Abolition reading treats it as irrelevant (state authority not derived from victim preferences); retribution might incorporate it as desert-validation signal. Unresolved whether family opposition undermines retributive reading's beneficiary claim.

Can a single jurisdiction hold deterrence AND retribution as complementary justifications (both/and) or are they mutually exclusive grounds? Empirically, jurisdictions invoke both, but no axiom contradiction declared between them — both accept execution as legitimate, differing only in justification source. This suggests licensed plurality rather than kernel contest between these two readings.

Do exoneration data (Innocence Project) undermine deterrence reading (execution of innocents destroys utility justification) or retribution reading (execution of innocents violates proportionality) or both? Abolition reading incorporates irreversibility as structural; other readings treat it as operational error-rate problem. Unresolved whether high error rates collapse deterrence/retribution into abolition.

Is global abolition trend (140+ countries abolished) a mountain (emerging jus cogens norm) or scaffold (contingent policy fashion)? If mountain, U.S. retention becomes anomalous piton. If scaffold, abolition reading's authority grounding weakens in jurisdictions without constitutional dignity clauses.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel identification is clean: three readings hold mutually exclusive axioms (retribution/abolition and deterrence/abolition pairs declared contradictory), emit structurally distinct constraints (different victim sets, beneficiary structures, authority grounds), and share the state-killing kernel as common substrate. Retribution/deterrence pair NOT axiom-contradictory (both accept execution legitimacy, differ only in justification source), but emit different observables and beneficiary structures warranting separate constraint stories. All three readings selected for generation.
